title: Left front door speaker removal and installation
introduction:
For Mustangs with the documented non-touchscreen SYNC controls, this guide covers removing and refitting the LH front-door midwoofer and woofer. The trim panel comes off first, including its window-switch assembly, electrical connections and latch cable.

I treat the door panel like a cupboard door with cables behind it: releasing the edges is only part of getting it safely out of the way. The preparation below explains those hidden attachments before you reach the speakers. Use the separate speaker drawings to identify each mounting arrangement and connector. This procedure covers physical removal and installation; the ordinary completion checks below do not replace electrical diagnosis.

requirements.category: Match the documented audio interface before starting

items.name: Non-touchscreen SYNC controls
items.detail: Before dismantling anything, confirm that the fitted non-touchscreen SYNC radio has the VOL/Power knob, RADIO button, TUNE knob and Seek controls described in the completion check. If the fitted system differs, stop before dismantling and obtain its matching owner operating instructions and applicable repair procedure. This article verifies the documented interface, not every SYNC variant.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury. Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

items.name: Protect eyes, ears and hands
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling components with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to follow these precautions may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Prepare tools for trim and small fasteners
items.detail: Have a trim-removal tool for lifting the window-switch bezel, tools that fit the mounting fasteners, and a torque tool suitable for the specified inch-pound tightening values. The switch drawing identifies the trim tool but does not specify fastener tool sizes.

items.name: Match the illustrated side
items.detail: The supporting trim-panel procedure shows LHD and the RH door, with RHD and LH described as similar. The window-switch procedure shows LHD and the LH door, with RHD and RH described as similar. Use the driver-side or passenger-side switch instructions according to the vehicle's steering configuration; LH alone does not identify which switch assembly is fitted.

requirements.category: Remove the door trim before reaching the speakers

items.name: Expose the upper trim bolt
items.detail: Remove the small cover inside the interior door-release handle recess, then remove the upper trim-panel bolt behind it. Its installation torque is 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). The cover's retaining features are visible in the [Front Door Trim Panel reference](#/document/G1692600).

items.name: Lift out the window-switch assembly
items.detail: Use the trim-removal tool to lift the window-switch bezel upward from the armrest and release its retaining clips. Lift out the switch and bezel together, then disconnect the window-switch electrical connector underneath. This common operation applies to both doors. Keep the [Front Door Window Control Switch reference](#/document/G1695936) available for its attachment views. Leave the switch attached to its bezel for this speaker job.

items.name: Remove the center bolt
items.detail: With the switch and bezel removed, remove the trim-panel center bolt exposed in the armrest opening. Its installation torque is 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm).

items.name: Remove the lower retainers
items.detail: Remove the retainers along the lower edge of the trim panel. Their installation torque is 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm). These threaded lower attachments are removed before releasing the perimeter clips and pin-type retainers.

items.name: Release the rear upper attachments
items.detail: At the rear upper edge, release the clip first, then the pin-type retainers farther down that rear edge. Move the rear upper portion of the trim panel outward, away from the door. Here, rear means the latch end of the door.

items.name: Release the rear and lower attachments
items.detail: Release the pin-type retainer near the lower rear corner, then the clip near the lower front speaker area. Move the rear and lower portion of the trim panel away from the door.

items.name: Release the front attachments
items.detail: At the hinge end of the panel, release the lower pin-type retainer near the speaker area, followed by both pin-type retainers farther up that edge. Move the panel away from the door as these attachments release.

items.name: Lift the panel clear and disconnect its remaining attachments
items.detail: Lift the trim panel up and out to release its upper edge from the door. Disconnect the panel electrical connectors, if equipped. Looking at the back of the panel, locate the latch cable behind the interior handle. Slide the cable-sheath fitting out through the opening in its retaining bracket, then detach the cable end from the handle. These are separate attachments: freeing the sheath fitting allows the cable end to be disconnected. Remove the panel once these connections are free. See [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600).

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal instructions for installation details as well; some refitting information appears alongside the removal actions.
edits.why: I check the tightening information before taking anything apart, so reassembly does not turn into a hunt through a pile of door trim.

edits.text:
Remove the front door trim panel to expose the speakers.
Refer to: [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600) (501-05 Interior Trim and Ornamentation, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: The preparation sequence above explains the concealed bolts, switch assembly, perimeter attachments and latch cable. Releasing those attachments in order lets the panel come away without treating its wiring and handle cable as carrying straps.

edits.text: Remove the mounting bolts, then remove the door midwoofer speaker.
edits.why: The midwoofer drawing shows the speaker in its roughly square mounting frame, with mounting bolts at the sides and lower edge. Keep the speaker supported as it comes away so its electrical connection remains accessible for the next action.

edits.text:
Disconnect the midwoofer electrical connector.
Installation bolt torque: 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm)
edits.why: The connector is at the lower-left edge of the speaker in the drawing. The tightening value applies to the mounting bolts during refitting, not to the electrical connector.

edits.text: Remove the mounting bolts, then remove the door woofer speaker.
edits.why: Use the woofer drawing to identify its large circular mounting flange and perimeter bolts. Keep the speaker supported while bringing its lower-left electrical connection within reach.

edits.text:
Disconnect the woofer electrical connector.
Installation bolt torque: 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm)
edits.why: Disconnecting the plug frees the speaker from the door harness. The tightening value belongs to the mounting bolts when the speaker is installed.

edits.text: Install by reversing the removal sequence. Reconnect each speaker electrical connector, position the speaker, and install its mounting bolts to the torque specified above. If both speakers were removed, refit the woofer before the midwoofer. Then reinstall the front door trim panel.
edits.why:
Transfer parts as necessary before refitting the trim. Reattach the latch cable to the handle mechanism and secure its housing in the bracket, then reconnect the panel electrical connectors, if equipped. Locate the panel's upper edge on the door and lower it into place. Reverse the perimeter release order: engage both upper front pin-type retainers, then the lower front retainer; engage the clip near the lower front speaker area, then the lower rear pin-type retainer; engage the rear-edge pin-type retainers, then the rear upper clip. Reinstall the lower threaded retainers and center bolt using their preparation-section torques. Reconnect the switch electrical connector and press the switch-and-bezel assembly back into the armrest so its retaining clips engage. Finally, install the upper trim bolt to its specified torque and refit its cover. Completion restores the speaker connections, handle cable, panel connectors and trim attachments.

After all wiring and trim are restored, keep the car parked in P for an automatic or a parked gear for a manual, with the parking brake applied, wheels chocked and the engine stopped. With the valid key inside, start from ignition OFF and press the start button without pressing either pedal to switch the ignition ON without starting the engine. For the documented non-touchscreen SYNC radio, if the audio is OFF, press the VOL/Power knob to turn it ON; if it has already resumed ON, leave it ON rather than toggling it. Press RADIO to select the radio band, then turn TUNE or press Seek to find a familiar station. Turn VOL to a comfortable level and listen for sound from the serviced door speakers. This is an ordinary function check, not fault isolation. After listening, press the audio Power control to turn the audio OFF. With ignition still in the known engine-off ON state, check the disturbed window switch: keep children and pets away and hands and objects clear of the glass; press the window switch to open the window and lift it to close. Confirm normal response without testing or overriding bounce-back. Press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to return the known ON state to OFF. With the ignition OFF, remove the key. Keep the parked gear, parking brake and wheel restraints in place. Gently open and close the door with its handle, confirming the interior handle releases the latch and the door latches normally without forcing it. These are ordinary checks of the disturbed controls and connections, not electrical diagnosis or door alignment. If sound, window response, handle action or retention is abnormal, stop before driving and keep ignition OFF/key out before reopening trim or checking a connector. See the [matching owner manual, Audio, Windows and Starting](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/Catalog/owner_information/2015-Mustang-Owners-Manual-version-1_om_EN-US_07_2014.pdf) for the fitted controls.

For SYNC remove unrelated switch replacement branch and clarify both upper hinge retainers and separate cable attachments; complete prior source/figure review retained, independent increment recorded separately.
